 Los Angeles Lakers Boston Celtics Washington Wizards Week 2 of NBA Cup Group Play is upon us on Friday with a massive nine-game slate, as several teams look to position themselves for a run into the quarterfinals.

 Dew’s Review: Make it six in a row for the Golden State Warriors behind another 29 points from Steph Curry. The Warriors star has this team in the thick of the playoff race, and there is the looming Jimmy Butler return that could make the Warriors even more dangerous in a suddenly open Western Conference. 
--> Dew’s Review: Make it six in a row for the Golden State Warriors behind another 29 points from Steph Curry. The Warriors star has this team in the thick of the playoff race, and there is the looming Jimmy Butler return that could make the Warriors even more dangerous in a suddenly open Western Conference. 
 Peter’s Point: The 76ers are mowing through Eastern Conference opponents, beating the New York Knicks twice (including in the NBA Cup last week), and they just took down the Detroit Pistons. The starting lineup of Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid may be the best in the league when healthy, and Philly gets another test against an East contender in the Cavs, who are 4-4 this season. Cleveland has some things to figure out on the wing this season after dealing for Peyton Watson, and this is a nice test for both squads as they battle for superiority in the East this season.

 Wizards guard Trae Young has a tough matchup on Friday night against an Atlanta Hawks defense that he faced on Wednesday and put up 18 points and six dimes against in a loss. Young was just 2-for-6 from 3 in that game. 
--> Wizards guard Trae Young has a tough matchup on Friday night against an Atlanta Hawks defense that he faced on Wednesday and put up 18 points and six dimes against in a loss. Young was just 2-for-6 from 3 in that game. 
 The Hawks are No. 1 in the league in opponent 3-pointers made per game and No. 3 in opponent 3-point percentage through the first two-plus weeks of the season, allowing less than 11 3s per game.
